pathways.title: Get mental health support
pathways.scope: Voluntary access to care. No complaint or private case is required.

steps.action: Find a centre and check local access.
steps.before: No referral or appointment normally needed; local arrangements vary.
steps.evidence: Explain the help you need. No documents or diagnosis are required by ClarityPath.
steps.timing: Check local hours. Not a crisis service.

steps.body: New South Wales Mental Health Line
steps.action: Contact the service for advice and referral.
steps.before: Concern about your own or someone else’s mental health; staff discuss needs.
steps.evidence: Staff ask for identity and contact details and information about your concerns.
steps.timing: 24 hours, every day. You do not have to try a centre first.

pathways.exceptions: These are alternative entry points. Ask about access, costs and waiting arrangements. Immediate danger: call 000.

pathways.title: Request discharge, then appeal refusal or non-response
pathways.scope: Civil detention under the Mental Health Act. Forensic orders need specialist advice.

steps.action: Ask orally or in writing for discharge and ask for the request to be recorded.
steps.before: A detained person can request discharge; obtain advice about carers or another appointed applicant.
steps.evidence: Request date, response and available order details.
steps.timing: The officer has 3 working days to decide.

steps.action: Contact the Tribunal to appeal refusal or non-determination.
steps.before: A refusal, or no decision within 3 working days of the request.
steps.evidence: Request and response or non-response dates; ask for help with the form.
steps.timing: A refusal permits appeal without waiting out the remaining 3 working days.

pathways.exceptions: Ask the Mental Health Advocacy Service about your status. A care complaint does not discharge you or pause an order.

pathways.title: Changing or ending a community treatment order
pathways.scope: Variation, revocation and appeal have different rules.

steps.body: Legal adviser, treating service or Mental Health Review Tribunal
steps.action: Obtain advice about the outcome sought and correct process.
steps.before: The Tribunal route requires material changed circumstances or relevant new information. Only the responsible facility can apply for variation.
steps.evidence: Order, treatment plan and explanation of changes or new information.
steps.timing: Use the order and Tribunal directions; seek prompt advice.

pathways.exceptions: The director of community treatment also has a revocation power. Court appeal is separate. Do not change treatment or ignore an order based on this summary.

pathways.title: Identify the order and correct appeal route
pathways.scope: Order-specific appeals; the Civil and Administrative Tribunal is not a general detention appeal forum.

steps.body: Mental Health Advocacy Service and relevant court or tribunal
steps.action: Take the order and reasons to a lawyer.
steps.before: Mental Health Review Tribunal determinations may go to the Supreme Court subject to court rules; specific orders have different routes.
steps.evidence: Order, reasons, receipt date and earlier applications.
steps.timing: Check applicable rules promptly. There is no universal appeal deadline here.

pathways.exceptions: Financial-management appeals can involve the Civil and Administrative Tribunal or Supreme Court. Magistrate-made community treatment orders have a Mental Health Review Tribunal appeal route. Complaints do not replace appeals.
